content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a chain dispute about Acts 2:30, so K-S2's restriction on the grounds for that verdict applies.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' could be read as barring underdetermination grounded on one verse's silence, or as barring any underdetermination involving an unstated point; the judge's words 'neither chain forces the other' are chain-balance language, so I weigh them as not single-verse silence.","why":"The judge's stated ground is that the competing chains do not force one another, not that a single verse fails to state the link or its contrary."}
